source_caption:
Y tu mamá también is one of those films that feels like a summer you’ll never really get back. It’s about friendship, growing up, desire, and those moments in life that seem ordinary at the time but end up staying with you long after they’re gone.

Directed by Alfonso Cuarón, the film follows two teenage friends, Julio and Tenoch, who go on a road trip with an older woman named Luisa. What starts off as a carefree adventure slowly turns into something more personal as their relationships and perspectives begin to change. The cinematography by Emmanuel Lubezki is a huge part of what makes this film so special. The natural lighting, long takes, and moving camera make everything feel incredibly real, almost like you’re travelling alongside the characters rather than watching a movie.

There’s so much happening beneath the surface, from friendship and class differences to the uncertainty of growing up. It’s funny, messy, and bittersweet in a way that feels true to life, and it leaves you thinking about how quickly certain chapters of our lives pass us by.

🎥: Y tu mamá también (2001)
Dir. Alfonso Cuarón

source_details.synopsis: Y tu mamá también (English: And Your Mama Too) is a 2001 Mexican coming-of-age erotic comedy-drama road film directed by Alfonso Cuarón, who co-wrote the screenplay with his brother Carlos Cuarón. The film follows two teenage boys who embark on a road trip with a woman in her late twenties and stars Diego Luna, Gael García Bernal, and Maribel Verdú, with narration by Daniel Giménez Cacho. Set in 1999, it unfolds against the backdrop of Mexico's political and economic realities at the close of seven uninterrupted decades of Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) presidencies and the rise of the opposition led by Vicente Fox.
